title: Accelerate exact four-flat requirement enumeration by 33x on a pinned corpus
body:
The four-flat decoder search spends most of its sampled runtime generating requirement pairs. This package replaces that routine's flat-subset enumeration with an exact branch on an uncovered label, extending DreamingOfClouds' existing Boolean feasibility method to **all minimal covers**. A residual-span lemma removes dominated covers without pairwise comparisons.

**Status: tooling improvement and scoped enumeration proof. No new κ or full four-flat-domain exclusion.** Answers [Discussion2954, route B](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2954#discussioncomment-18975620).

| Same-input check | Original | Replacement | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 25,001 distinct residual masks | 128.91 s | 3.91 s | 33.00× |
| Full 12-pair sample, including unchanged setup | 246.70 s | 117.86 s | 2.09× |
| Requirement-generation stage in that run | see receipt | see receipt | 32.77× |

Both implementations produce identical minimal-cover sets, all 11 exported requirement records, all 5,509 closure leaves and the complete rank histogram. The full replay regenerates the 25,001-case corpus from 25,991 actual calls. The proof bounds the search tree by 1,023 nodes when `(c,d)=(4,5)` and establishes minimal-antichain equivalence for arbitrary finite label sets; the timing table is only this machine and sample.

Verification passed: registered Python 3.12 replay; independent explicit-subspace oracle on all 2,048 F2^3 subset/capacity cases; seven rejecting controls; sanitizer-trap kernel replay; known span-five positive outer control; optimized Python 3.14 fast-kernel/oracle replay from a read-only Git-free export; all 19 committed files match tested bytes. No independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/two-flat-cover-branching/verify.py --work /tmp/two-flat-replay
```

Use a fresh work directory, Python 3.12+ and a GNU-C11-capable `cc`. Expected final line: `PASS_TWO_FLAT_COVER_BRANCHING`. The registered manifest splits kernel and outer replays into bounded commands.

Scientific base `afc158a25ef3e0bd80de81d1eb5339f0dace118e`; branch synchronized to `a23bdc1b07be96bea0101d44ae27d14de67a79ed` before publication. Exact source: DreamingOfClouds' help package at `1b25759bff5486293a9083ebbe0097b5f6642e08`. Credit that source's existing `dfs4` feasibility routine and #2816/#2826/#2862 lineage. Tekalign with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0.

Only `research/two-flat-cover-branching/` is added: 19 files, 1,089 added text lines, under 1 MB including compressed inputs. Frozen sources, shared code, `upstream/` and the selected frontier are untouched. The complete outer census remains too large; catalogue/orbit completeness, RRC and original integer-rank obligations are not newly discharged. This is a useful research accelerator, not a claim that the class-C problem is solved. Recent κ constructions #2957/#2966/#2969 concern different supplier changes.
